references.text: A strong parallel event where a host protects his guests from the men of the city who intend to harm them, in the story of the Levite at Gibeah.
Lot chooses to settle near Sodom, which explains the accusation 'the one came as a stranger' (bā-lāḡûr) in 19:9.
Jesus' warning that it will be better for Sodom than for cities that reject his messengers, linked to the themes of hospitality and justice.
Peter's reference to Lot as a righteous man tormented by the immoral conduct of the lawless in Sodom highlights the contrast between the righteous and the ungodly.
Lot sits at the city gate, suggesting a judicial role in the city – relevant to the accusation 'will he judge and judge' (vayishpōṭ šāp̄ōṯ).
Both show how the ungodly use false accusations of violation to justify violence against a righteous man.
The psalm formulates the principle that those who hate the righteous are punished, as Lot experiences in practice.
